source.title: RAS: Measuring LLM Safety Through Refusal Alignment
source.authors: Changhui Huang; Yan-Lun Chen; Chia-Mu Yu; Wei-Bin Lee

record.tranche_reason: Applies reference-derived refusal directions to different model variants and families and reports alignment and output-level safety results; it does not perform the original causal ablation or addition intervention.
record.gate_note: The paper extracts difference-in-means directions and measures alignment against them, but does not ablate or add a direction. Numerical values used only to select layer windows are omitted. Target-model RAS and safety comparisons are shown in figures without numerical values; the text gives aggregate trends but not model-specific numbers.
record.test_reason: The study extracts a difference-in-means (unsafe minus safe) refusal direction from each family's official instruct model and measures how strongly fine-tuned, uncensored and abliterated variants of that family align with it (Tables 1, 3, 4). It then compares this with each model's HEx-PHI attack success rate (ASR). This bears on V6 (the direction carries across model variants) and, through the released abliterated models' ASR, on V2. It runs no ablation or addition, so V1 is not tested. It is a new setting (a safety-audit metric).
record.authors_conclusion: Broadly correct. The authors conclude that alignment of hidden states with a reference model's refusal direction (calibrated as RAS) separates aligned from uncensored and abliterated variants within each family, tracks ASR at the family level rather than as a strict per-model ranking, and is about 200× faster than judge-based evaluation. They add that it needs family-specific calibration and white-box access, and that it may miss safety implemented through other mechanisms, possibly needing a multi-directional extension.
record.recipe_differences: Uses a harmful/unsafe-minus-safe mean activation direction, but extracts it from a safety-aligned reference model and measures cosine alignment over selected layer windows. It does not perform causal ablation or activation addition.
record.method_sensitivity: The selected layer window is family-specific: Llama 22–30, Gemma 27–29, and Qwen 22–26. Raw cosine scores require family-specific calibration. The authors note a Gemma variant whose alignment and ASR do not rank consistently.
record.problems: No causal intervention establishes mediation. The output-level ASR evaluation uses a single named judge model; no uncertainty estimates are reported. No general-capability evaluation tests whether abilities are preserved. The paper notes a Gemma variant with lower raw refusal alignment but lower ASR.
record.rows_left_out: Omitted model-specific numerical values for target-model RAS and 100 × (1 − ASR) because Figures 4, 11, and 12 provide figures without numerical values. Also omitted layer-window selection values because they are used to choose the scoring window.

untested.parts: No ablation or activation addition and no capability check. The direction is only used as a measurement axis.
The study does not perform or describe the weight edits. It evaluates third-party released abliterated models and does not test whether other abilities are kept.
No transfer across languages, from base to instruct models, or across families (directions are family-specific). No causal test that the reference direction mediates refusal in the variants.
Multi-directional refusal is only raised as a possibility in the Limitations, not tested.
One Gemma reasoning-distill model is scored, but there is no causal V1 test in a reasoning model.
Jailbreak-prompt alignment is measured, but there is no test that attacks work by suppressing the direction, and no adversarial training.

missing.what: HEx-PHI ASR for the non-abliterated variants, needed to judge whether alignment tracks refusal. Llama: Configurable 0.127, Nemotron 0.281, Fireplace2 0.358, Rupesh Uncensored 0.633, DarkIdol 0.936, Lexi 0.939. Gemma: reasoning-distill 0.076, document-writer 0.339. Qwen: MAGIC 0.139, shisa 0.415, Orion Uncensored 0.976.
Correct Gemma unsafe scores: mlabonne abliterated -0.044, YanLabs normpreserve -0.090 (the rows show -0.090 and -0.153).

record.verdict_notes: No causal intervention is run. The V6 evidence is correlational: alignment with the reference direction versus ASR across fine-tuned variants. Reference-model rows are the baseline, not tests. The study does not create the abliterated models, so the V2 evidence rests on third-party edits with no capability check. ASR uses a single judge (SORRY-Bench Mistral-7B) with no uncertainty reported. The text gives a 216.88× average speedup but Table 2 reports 210.13×. The reader's 'partial' states for lower-alignment variants misread V6: lower alignment in less-safe variants is the expected pattern if the direction carries over.

versions.untested_parts: No causal removal or addition of the direction, and no test that other abilities remain intact.
The study evaluates named released abliterated variants but does not itself perform or describe the weight edit that produced each variant.
No test that jailbreak attacks suppress the direction or that training against ablation improves robustness.
No comparison of a single direction with an affine, cone, or multidirectional representation.
No separate measurement of harmfulness judgment and refusal decision.
Tests reference directions on variants within each family; does not test transfer across languages, from base to instruct models, or use of one direction across model families.
No controlled variation of refusal-training method or timing.
Includes one reasoning-distill model as a model variant but does not test whether the causal V1 claim holds in reasoning models.
